turnaround_reason: The former ASGN, rebranded to Everforth in April 2026, is the 4th-largest US IT staffing/solutions firm (commercial + federal). Stock is down ~52% over the past year as DOGE-driven federal spending cuts hit the government segment and a soft IT hiring cycle pressured commercial staffing. The recovery thesis: a profitable, FCF-generative solutions/consulting mix (not just body-shop staffing) at a trough multiple with a heavy insider-buying cluster.
bullish_points: Genuinely profitable and cash-generative: GAAP profit margin ~2%, ~$213M FCF, trailing P/E ~16.7x / forward ~7.5x - not a cash-burner
Cluster of open-market insider PURCHASES in April 2026 (Matin $193K, Hawthorne $100K, Callaghan $104K, plus several directors) - the strongest insider signal in today's batch
Cheap on solutions-business metrics: ~0.73x book, EV/EBITDA ~7.9x, EV/revenue ~0.68x
Rebrand toward 'technology and digital engineering at scale' repositions away from commodity staffing toward higher-margin work
Q2 EPS beat (+11.4%); commercial segment revenue edged up while the market feared worse
bearish_points: Federal segment directly exposed to DOGE / government-efficiency cuts - a policy-driven headwind outside management's control
Revenue declining (-1.3%) with both segments soft (commercial +0.5%, federal -1.1%) - no top-line inflection yet
Price is ~132% of the 100d MA and well off the $16.9 low - much of the easy bounce may already be in ('basing' but extended)
Analyst mean target ($27.5) sits BELOW spot ($32.4) - the Street sees it as roughly fair-to-rich here, recommendation 'none'
Leverage moderate-high: debt/equity ~83%, $1.5B debt vs $153M cash
yfinance news feed empty; thesis leans on one web pass + insider filings
catalyst: Q3 FY2026 earnings on Oct 28, 2026 - read on federal-segment stabilization post-DOGE and commercial IT-hiring recovery
suggested_trade: Spot only, small starter, and prefer buying weakness given the mean analyst target sits below spot. The April insider-buy cluster is the real reason to watch it; let a pullback toward the mid-$20s improve the entry.
key_risk: Federal spending cuts deepen and commercial IT hiring stays weak, so revenue keeps sliding while the stock - already above analyst targets and well off its lows - gives back the bounce.
would_skip_if: Federal segment revenue decline accelerates on the Oct 28 print, or you're unwilling to buy above the Street's mean target.
